sections.what_happened: Baqaei: any US attack will be met with retaliation — 'the era of the US carrying out attacks and withdrawing without consequences was over'; Iran's response will be 'equal in force' at minimum, if not stronger. Dismissed claims Washington conveyed a message expecting Tehran not to respond ('illusion'). Denied ongoing nuclear negotiations with Washington. Addressed claims of a possible US attack on Pickaxe Mountain (Kuh-e Kolang). Separately on Munir visit: talks 'mainly focused on bilateral relations', dismissed speculation about delivered threats; and: 'We live with this possibility day and night, and we cannot rule it out, even as we speak' (on a return to US strikes).
sections.what_verified: AA Tuesday update, Al Arabiya Farsi IG reel (59K likes/1.8K comments; clip date 2026-10-20 matches presser), ISNA/Mehr context on Munir meetings.
sections.what_disputed: Denial of 'ongoing nuclear negotiations' is contradicted in tone by Qatar's Oct-20 claim that Iran-US JCPOA engagement is 'ongoing' (covered 1400-06) — the gap is between formal talks vs back-channel contact.
sections.why_matters: On the record, in Tehran, hours after Pakistan's army chief landed and the day after Lavrov left: Iran's spokesman ended the ambiguity — any American attack gets answered, equal or stronger, and the 'don't respond' message Washington allegedly sent is an 'illusion.' Iran-side framing: when the threats are this explicit, the Council's silence IS a position — and Tehran is done assuming it survives one.
sections.context: Background: Iran FM spox Baqaei Tuesday presser: retaliation doctrine hardened, no nuclear talks with Washington

totw_analysis: Our read: On the record, in Tehran, hours after Pakistan's army chief landed and the day after Lavrov left: Iran's spokesman ended the ambiguity — any American attack gets answered, equal or stronger, and the 'don't respond' message Washington allegedly sent is an 'illusion.' Iran-side framing: when the threats are this explicit, the Council's silence IS a position — and Tehran is done assuming it survives one. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Tehran says the era of unanswered strikes is OVER and it's ruling out no scenario — while Qatar insists back-channel talks are alive. Is Iran closing the door on diplomacy, or is the hard talk the price of a seat at the table?
